objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of smart healthcare interventions on disease activity, self-efficacy, self-management, functional levels, and quality of life in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients, as well as any associated adverse events.
inclusion_criteria: Eligibility criteria were defined using population, intervention, control, outcome, and study design. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials focused on smart health interventions for adults with rheumatoid arthritis. RA could be defined by established classification criteria (such as the 1987 ACR criteria or the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria) or by a physician's clinical diagnosis. Eligible interventions included smart healthcare approaches that enabled symptom tracking and self-management support via health applications or online platforms, as well as telemedicine and teleconsultation services; common functions included automated symptom tracking, regular remote follow-up, and self-management support. Studies had to report outcome data specifically attributable to the smart healthcare component.
exclusion_criteria: The accessible main text explicitly excluded studies that did not report outcome data specifically attributable to the smart healthcare component. Under the stated PICOS/RCT eligibility framework, studies outside adult rheumatoid arthritis randomized controlled trials of smart healthcare interventions were also ineligible.
pmid_query: ("Arthritis, Rheumatoid"[MeSH Terms] OR "rheumatoid arthritis"[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Telemedicine"[MeSH Terms] OR telemedicine[Title/Abstract] OR "digital health"[Title/Abstract] OR mHealth[Title/Abstract]) AND ("Randomized Controlled Trial"[Publication Type] OR randomized[Title/Abstract])
selection_evidence: Results/PRISMA explicitly state that 18 RCTs were included: [18,19,29-44]. Table 1 lists 18 study reports whose first authors/years align to those same references: Song (18), Li LC (19), Knudsen (29), Skovsgaard (30), Seppen 2023 (31), Pers (32), de Thurah (33), Li C (34), Lee (35), Pouls (36), Ferwerda 2017 (37), Andonian (38), Seppen 2022 (39), Bernard (40), Ferwerda 2018 (41), Zuidema (42), Allam (43), and Rodriguez Sanchez-Laulhe (44). Cross-checking the reference list shows these are literature citations in journals rather than websites, datasets, or software repositories.
notes: The manuscript appears to count some companion/economic-evaluation reports as separate included study reports (notably refs 30, 31, and 41); because the Results section and Table 1 explicitly treat them as included, they are retained here. The country-summary sentence appears to contain a typo: Canada is labeled [31], but Table 1 and the reference list indicate the Canada study is ref 19. The full text of S1/S3 supplemental DOCX files was not text-extracted in the accessible workspace, so the criteria wording and pmid_query are taken from, or reconstructed from, the detailed main-text Methods.
